payload.headline: NVIDIA at 156.14 on report day after reported CEO exit; hold, no trade

summary.thesis: NVIDIA is a grade-A business priced below every fair-value method, but the price assumes high margins hold, and today's report and a reported leadership change come first.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add only after the report if margins hold. Swing: no trade until the 2026-11-17 report is out.
summary.act_at: Add at 150.22 if margin holds; reassess near 218.73

payload.happening: The stock fell 4.12% to 156.14 and is in a downtrend, below its 20-day (195.64), 50-day (213.15) and 200-day (203.75) averages. Quarterly results are due on 2026-11-17. Interim CEO Colette Kress presents them, after Jensen Huang's resignation was reported. NVIDIA announced a board committee to oversee national security and export controls, and U.S. agencies reportedly began investigating partner Megaspeed in 2024.
payload.business: The business numbers are strong. Revenue for the last 12 months was 303.0B, up from 165.2B. Quarterly sales growth sped up to 105.85% from 73.21% two quarters earlier. Operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%, and free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) reached 127.0B, up from 72.0B. Two things could change the business itself. First, margin is at the top of its 5-year range (16–65%), and peaks like this often fade. Second, unpaid customer bills grew 127% while sales grew 106%, which can mean sales were pulled forward or customers are paying more slowly. Export-control and China headlines (reported) could affect demand if they turn into rules (general knowledge), so they are a business risk and not only a mood risk. The reported CEO exit, the new committee and $946.6M of insider sales outside pre-set plans are governance and sentiment issues. They do not change demand or cash today. Balance sheet risk is low: net cash is 23.2B and liquidity is 56.6B.

worth.text: At 156.14 the stock trades at 19.7 times trailing earnings and 9.9 times next year's expected earnings. Price-to-sales (P/S, price divided by yearly sales) is 12.4, below the peer median of 15.7 and at the 4.0th percentile of its own 5-year history. The discounted cash flow (DCF) model, which values future cash in today's money, gives 189.87 / 220.46 / 261.33 (bear / base / bull). Own-history P/S gives 217.35 to 411.04. The current price assumes free cash flow starts growing about 21.0% a year. At 20% starting growth the value is 150.22, and at 30% it is 218.73. So the gap between methods depends mostly on how fast cash flow grows at the start. Margin matters just as much: if operating margin falls to 48% the value drops to 112.91, and at 32% to 75.59. The stock looks cheap only if today's margin holds.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near 65.21% rather than fading toward 48%.

bull: P/S of 12.4 is below the peer median of 15.7 and sits at the 4.0th percentile of its own 5-year history.
Quarterly sales growth sped up to 105.85% from 73.21% two quarters ago, and free cash flow rose to 127.0B from 72.0B.
Analysts' next-year EPS estimate of 15.84 rose 23.2% over 90 days, which puts the stock at 9.9 times next year's earnings.
bear: Unpaid customer bills rose 127% while sales rose 106%, a possible sign of sales pulled forward or customers paying more slowly.
Operating margin of 65.21% is at the top of its 5-year range. At 48% the cash-flow value falls to 112.91, well below the price.
The trend is down, with the price below the 50-day average of 213.15. There is no support level below the price, and insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans.

levels.what: Today's close. It implies about 21.0% starting cash-flow growth, which recent results have beaten. That is enough to keep holding, but not enough to add hours before the report.
Value at 20% starting growth, the low end of the range. Add here only if the report shows operating margin near 65.21% and customer bills growing in line with sales.
Value at 30% starting growth, the high end of the range and close to the DCF base of 220.46. Near here most of the upside is used up, so reassess and consider trimming.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the business is grade A, but the committee call is 'Hold', and the macro, technical and risk views are all negative. The value case supports owning the stock. The receivables warning and the report today argue against adding first.

swing.why: There is no support below the price to place a stop under, and resistance sits just above at 163.9–169.14. Options price a 9.7% move by 2026-11-20, almost a full daily range (ATR 9.85) and more, so the report can jump past any stop.

decision.timing: Take no action before the 2026-11-17 report. Implied volatility (the move options expect) is 103.6, against 53.9 actually realized, a ratio of 1.92, so the market expects a big move. After the report, compare revenue with 108.7B, EPS with 2.47 and next-quarter guidance with 124.9B before acting at 150.22 or 218.73.

change_mind: Add: the report shows revenue at or above 108.7B, operating margin near 65.21% and customer bills growing no faster than sales, with the price at or below 150.22.
Move to trim or avoid: guidance comes in below the 124.9B next-quarter estimate, or margin moves toward 48%, where value falls to 112.91.
Reconsider a swing entry: a close above the 169.14 top of the first resistance zone after the report, which would break the pattern of lower highs.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold with no swing trade, because nothing new on the business has come out before the 2026-11-17 report. The fair-value range moved to 150.22–218.73 from 151.37–224.74, and options now price a 9.7% move with implied volatility at 103.6.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
